global_caption: The video consists of 6 shots and is a realistic-style, warm-toned balcony gardening tutorial. The overall atmosphere is warm and fresh, with colors dominated by off-white, terracotta brown, and plant tender green. The camera movement is steady and smooth, with lighting primarily using natural soft light from the balcony, occasionally featuring slight backlighting from the window.
shot1: Shot 1 opens with a direct cut, using a medium-long shot at eye level. In the foreground, a row of balcony plants is softly blurred to create spatial depth. In the midground, a table clearly displays flower pots, clay pebbles, moist potting soil, mint seeds, and a small spray bottle. The background features a window frame glowing with warm light and gently swaying sheer curtains. The composition centers on the workbench, with moderate depth of field ensuring all materials are clearly visible. A pair of hands belonging to a middle-aged woman enters the frame naturally from the edges, lightly touching each item in turn as an introduction.
shot2: Shot 2 cuts directly from the previous shot, switching to a close-up overhead composition. Sunlight strikes diagonally from the rear side, creating soft highlights on the edges of the clay pebbles. Two hands first evenly spread the clay pebbles across the bottom of the pot; the pebbles roll and make slight collisions as they fall. Then, moist nutrient soil is added until the pot is eight-tenths full, with the soil's shape gradually becoming smoother as the hands level it.
shot3: The third shot enters with a hard cut to a close-up overhead view, focusing tightly on the fingers, soil surface, and tiny seeds. A shallow depth of field softens the background edges, while warm natural light highlights the granular texture of the slightly moist soil. Fingers gently press into the soil, creating a visible shallow groove, followed by evenly scattering mint seeds and lightly covering them with an extremely thin layer of fine soil. In the composition, the flowerpot occupies the lower half of the frame, while the watering can enters from the right, creating a diagonal motion trajectory.
